BeforeSideTurnStart.maps_to: on_player_turn_start (shuriken.py:27-28) -- the sim's PRE-draw turn-start slot, executed-confirmed to sit AFTER the block clear and the energy reset (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order)
BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: Shuriken.cs:90-99 resets AttacksPlayedThisTurn from BeforeSideTurnStart, which is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 9 -- BEFORE the block clear. The sim's on_player_turn_start is step ~12-13, after the clear and the energy reset. Only a counter reset happens here, and nothing can read the counter in the intervening window: the only reader is on_card_played and the play phase does not open until step 28, so the counter is 0 at every point either codebase can observe it. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the slot genuinely differs and a future effect placed between steps 9 and 13 would expose it -- the same reasoning and the same verdict as relic/brilliant_scarf's and relic/beating_remnant's BeforeSideTurnStart entries (binding rule 3). Also note C#'s `if (!participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)) return;` (Shuriken.cs:92-95) is structurally satisfied: on_player_turn_start is dispatched only for the player side. Rule 7: turn_structure.json, hooks.py and combat.py are not hashed here.

AfterCardPlayed.rationale: Shuriken.cs:101-113 increments on an Attack owned by the relic's owner while the combat is in progress, then applies PowerVar<StrengthPower>(1) whenever the running count is a multiple of CardsVar(3). shuriken.py:31-39 mirrors it clause for clause: the Attack type check, the `% self.ATTACKS == 0` test on the post-increment count, and PowerCmd.apply(..., StrengthPower, 1, applier=self.player) against C#'s `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(ctx, Owner.Creature, Strength.BaseValue, Owner.Creature, null)` -- same applier, same target. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py shuriken): four Strikes give counter 1/2/3/4 and Strength 0/0/1/1; a Defend does not advance the counter. The two C# guards the sim omits are both structurally satisfied -- `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner` is single-player (see guard N2) and `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress` holds because on_card_played is a combat hook and combat.py breaks the play loop once the fight is decided. Rule 7: cmds.py, powers.py and combat.py are not hashed here.

AfterCombatEnd.maps_to: no counterpart; the sim's only reset is on_player_turn_start (shuriken.py:27-28)
AfterCombatEnd.rationale: Shuriken.cs:123-129 zeroes AttacksPlayedThisTurn (and the two display fields) at combat end as well as at turn start; the sim keeps only the turn-start half. The stale value is provably unreadable and this was EXECUTED rather than reasoned (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py shuriken): the relic instance carries counter = 4 out of combat 1, and the same instance in a fresh CombatState reports counter = 0 and Strength 0 after turn setup, because on_player_turn_start's reset is UNCONDITIONAL (`self._attacks_this_turn = 0`, no guard) and runs before the play phase opens. This is PROMPT.md bug class 13's required trace-to-the-first-reader, and it is the relic/art_of_war shape -- contrast this batch's self_forming_clay, whose turn-start write is a consume-then-clear and therefore is NOT safe, and relic/belt_buckle, which has no turn-start reset to fall back on. Rule 7: relics/art_of_war.py, relics/belt_buckle.py and audit/records/relic/self_forming_clay.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: C# has NO `cardPlay.IsAutoPlay` exclusion, so the sim counting auto-plays is CORRECT here (PROMPT.md class 29)
guards.rationale: Checked deliberately because the sibling relic/brilliant_scarf's LIVE gap G1 is exactly the opposite: BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87 opens with `if (cardPlay.IsAutoPlay) return;` and its port counts every play. Shuriken.cs:101-113 has no such clause -- read the whole method -- so an auto-played Attack DOES advance the game's counter, and shuriken.py:30-33 counting it is right. PROMPT.md class 29 records this trap for RainbowRing/RazorTooth; Shuriken is a fourth site. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py shuriken): an auto-played Strike through CombatState.auto_play_card leaves the counter at 1, matching C#. Copying the Scarf's verdict would have filed a false gap. Rule 7: BrilliantScarf.cs, relics/brilliant_scarf.py and combat.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner` (Shuriken.cs:103) -- the sim's on_card_played carries no owner
guards.rationale: A multiplayer guard: another player's Attack must not advance this Shuriken. The sim's hook signature is on_card_played(card) with no player, and CombatState holds one player, so the condition is unsatisfiable. Noted in the mapping per the shared contract's scope section rather than filed as a divergence.

guards.what: N3: the constants -- CardsVar(3) read as IntValue (Shuriken.cs:106) and PowerVar<StrengthPower>(1m) read as BaseValue (line 110)
guards.rationale: ATTACKS = 3 and the literal 1 (shuriken.py:21, :38) match, and there is no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in Shuriken.cs, so both are the pinned non-ascension values. Re-read against the C# per PROMPT.md class 19 rather than trusting the port's docstring.

guards.what: N4: the modulo semantics -- the counter is never reset ON activation, so the relic fires on every 3rd Attack, not once
guards.rationale: Worth pinning because the obvious alternative implementation (reset to 0 on trigger) would look equivalent and is not: C# keeps incrementing and tests `AttacksPlayedThisTurn % intValue == 0` (Shuriken.cs:107), so attacks 3, 6 and 9 in one turn each grant Strength. shuriken.py:34 does the same. EXECUTED: the probe's four-Strike run shows Strength arriving on attack 3 and not on attack 4. The `_isActivating` flag C# also keeps is display-only (Shuriken.cs:48-60, :76-88, :115-121) and drives DisplayAmount, not the trigger.
